initiative.title: Multi-scale dependency view
initiative.summary: Replace the crude TS-only file dependency graph with a multi-scale, focus-centered view for TypeScript and Python: folders/modules with bundled edges when zoomed out, accurate edges when zoomed in, 30-50 labeled items on screen, uniform boxes, rectilinear routing that never crosses nodes.
initiative.next_action: M2: graph contract endpoint + full TS resolution

claims.statement: Zoomed out, the view shows folders/modules with bundled aggregate edges; spaghetti must be avoided.
When zoomed to something specific, render accurate edges to every relevant place.
Aim for 30-50 labeled items on screen; smaller items may render unlabeled.
Focus-centered layout: whatever the user expressed interest in sits in the center.
Flows render left-to-right or top-to-bottom; call-chain/hop rendering is deferred. Current goal is immediate seams.
Uniform box sizes, clean text, rectilinear edges that never cross nodes, minimized crossings, bundled edges sharing a path (1-2px apart).
Must work for both TypeScript and Python.
Zoomed out, collapse many real edges into a few aggregate edges showing broad themes; detail appears only as the user zooms in.
Grouping levels come from folders or module boundaries (not auto-clustering).
Focused layout is three columns: dependents left, focus center, dependencies right (resolves X1).
Detail changes by click-to-drill: clicking a folder expands it and makes it the focus, splitting its bundled edges; breadcrumbs go back out; scroll only magnifies.
The focused item expands into symbols. On the other side of each edge, show the specific symbols involved when they fit; otherwise keep them bundled as files.
Focus is set from the treemap selection or by clicking in the graph.
Future: a symbol-focused explorer/search (e.g. popular or commonly used symbols) that the treemap cannot offer. Not in the first version, but the design must not preclude it.
The other side of focus edges shows the specific function/symbol in the importing file that uses the focus symbol (usage tracking in bodies, TS and Python).

Fill the screen with nodes. More than 3 columns is allowed: incoming on the left, outgoing on the right, positioned by interconnectedness. Group by folder or aggregate only when it still does not fit. Goal: exploring how ALL things interconnect.
Neighbor-to-neighbor edges (not touching focus) are drawn faintly.
Hidden/collapsed by default: external packages, tests, type-only imports; barrel/__init__ re-exports are passed through to the defining file.
Extra columns come from layering within each side: still 1-hop only, and a dependent that imports another dependent sits further out.

Target stays ~30-50 boxes, packed to the screen aspect ratio. Use as many columns as needed (e.g. 5); do not waste width holding to 3 strict columns; the focus column can be narrow when it holds one node.
First proof: layout + routing on existing TS data (folder overview, drill, focus columns, orthogonal bundled routing). Then Python resolution, then symbol usage.
Must stay fast on ~2k-file repos; graph built on first open and cached with the existing analysis cache.

conflicts.statement: Focus-centered (radial-ish) layout vs. directional L->R/T->B flow.
Fill the screen with nodes (C16) vs. 30-50 labeled items (C3).
conflicts.status: resolved: ~30-50 boxes packed to aspect ratio across as many layered columns as needed (C20)

shape.appetite: Replacement dependency view plus one language-neutral graph contract (TS + Python). No call-graph/data-flow beyond which function references an imported name.
shape.problem: The current view is a flat TS-only file graph laid out in one ELK pass with post-layout repositioning; it spaghettis, crosses nodes, and has no hierarchy, Python, or usage data.
shape.recommended_shape: Server emits finest-level hierarchical graph (folder>file>symbol, flagged edges); client does roll-up/budget view model -> ELK layered with partitions, fixed sizes, orthogonal routing, mergeEdges -> bundling offsets -> render. New component behind toggle until parity.

success_moves.move: Split into three pure stages (view model, layout, routing/render) and never reposition after layout.
success_moves.benefit: Removes main cause of node-crossing edges; each stage fixture-testable in vitest.

success_moves.move: Client-side roll-up over one finest-level graph contract shared by TS and Python.
success_moves.benefit: Drill is local and instant; languages differ only in extraction.

success_moves.move: First proof on existing TS /dependencies data with no backend change.
success_moves.benefit: Proves the riskiest part (routing quality) before investing in Python/usage extraction.

success_moves.move: Exhaust ELK options (partitioning, mergeEdges, fixed sizes, orthogonal) before a custom router; libavoid-js/custom router is a gated spike.
success_moves.benefit: Avoids building a router unless evidence demands it.

success_moves.move: Automated geometry assertions: edge-node intersections = 0, crossing count, box count, aspect fill.
success_moves.benefit: Turns visual goals into regressions tests rather than eyeballing.

success_moves.move: Ship new view behind a toggle beside the old component.
success_moves.benefit: Rollback is a toggle; old view retired at parity.

first_proof.question: Can ELK layered (partitions, fixed sizes, orthogonal, mergeEdges) plus a bundling offset pass produce 0 node-crossing, bundled, <=50-box focus and overview layouts on real TS data?
first_proof.artifact: View model + rollup + ELK layout on current /dependencies data for srcly; focus fixtures client/src/components and metricsStore.tsx; geometry checks + screenshots
first_proof.decision_rule: 0 node crossings and readable bundling at <=50 boxes -> keep ELK, proceed to graph contract + Python. Otherwise run the router spike before more work.

rabbit_holes: ELK layered may not pack sides to viewport aspect ratio; may need custom column wrapping
mergeEdges gives overlap, not 1-2px offset bundles; offset pass needed
Python absolute import resolution across package roots / src layouts
Function-level usage tracking (name references in bodies, aliasing, attribute access on module imports)
Compound focus (symbols inside file box) with ELK hierarchy handling

dependencies.name: Custom grid + channel layout (replaced elkjs)

first_proof_role.rationale: The library itself is the risk under test.

dependencies.rollout: behind New dependency view toggle; swappable behind layoutView

fast_local_loop.command: pnpm --dir client test -- deps; cd server && uv run pytest -k dependency_graph
fast_local_loop.failure_injection: synthetic fixtures (80-neighbor rollup, barrel chains, odd python layouts)
fast_local_loop.fidelity_proof: screenshots of running app on srcly at 1440/1024px

milestones.title: New focus view renders today's TS data with clean routing
milestones.outcome: Toggle shows folder overview + three-sided focus on srcly with 0 node crossings, <=50 boxes.
milestones.proof: vitest view-model + geometry checks on fixtures; screenshots
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: New view behind toggle; old view default.
evidence: client/src/viz/deps/*.test.ts: 0 node crossings on 5 focus fixtures
Spike P1 resolved: ELK dropped for custom layout after user steer + measurements

milestones.title: Language-neutral graph contract with full TS resolution
milestones.outcome: New /dependency-graph endpoint with hierarchy and flagged importer->imported edges; barrels resolved; filters.
milestones.proof: pytest per resolution case; M1 geometry tests on contract fixtures
milestones.rollback: Point client back to adapted /dependencies payload.

milestones.title: Python fills the same contract
milestones.outcome: Python repos render with correct seams and counts.
milestones.proof: pytest on synthetic layouts + srcly server/
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Python simply absent if extractor disabled.

milestones.title: Focus expands into symbols with function-level usage
milestones.outcome: Focused file shows symbols; other side shows using functions when budget allows.
milestones.proof: metricsStore fixture shows SortHeader -> HOTSPOT_METRICS; geometry checks pass
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: Without symbol edges, view falls back to file-level.

milestones.title: Retire the old view
milestones.outcome: Single dependency view; old component, toggle, and route removed.

cut_line: multi-hop flows / call chains / semantic zoom

history.event: Initiative created from request plus repository survey.
Shape brief written; ELK-first with gated router spike; first proof on existing TS data.
Implementation plan written: 5 milestones, M1 client-only routing proof.
M1 built. ELK tried, then replaced with custom grid+channel layout (user steer: avoid endless parameter tuning). Spike P1 resolved.

questions.question: Focused layout: 3 columns / radial / layered T-B?
Zoom model: click drill / continuous semantic / both?
questions.answer: Implied zoom drives aggregation (edges collapse when zoomed out)
questions.effect: carried to round 2 as understanding check

questions.question: Zoomed-out boxes: folders / language modules / auto-cluster?
(re-asked) layout/zoom/finest/focus source
questions.answer: 3 columns; click to drill; focus expands to symbols, receiving side shows symbols if possible else files; focus from treemap + graph click; symbol explorer later

questions.question: Column overflow
questions.answer: Fill screen, >3 columns ok, position by interconnectedness, aggregate last

questions.question: Fill screen vs label cap
questions.answer: Keep 30-50 boxes; pack columns to aspect ratio, e.g. 5 columns; no wasted space for strict 3
